questions.stem: In the conventional historical classification of programming-language generations, which generation is associated with declarative logic, constraints, AI and expert systems?
questions.hint: Use the cited language rules to separate the purpose of each construct from its implementation details.
sources: MOE Computer Science Exit Exam · 2016 · Question 17

answer.explanation: The question uses the historical generation taxonomy, rather than asking which languages can implement AI. The note associates fifth-generation languages with logic, constraints and expert systems. Second generation refers to assembly, third to general high-level languages, and fourth to query languages and application generators. Those other languages can be used within AI applications, but that does not change their generation category.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Fifth generation is the historical logic/constraints and expert-system category.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Second generation denotes symbolic assembly.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Fourth generation denotes query languages and application generators.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Third generation includes general high-level languages such as C++ and Java.

evidence.quote: Machine instructions are conventionally first generation; symbolic assembly is second; general high-level languages such as C++ and Java are third. Database query and application generators such as SQL are conventionally fourth generation. Fifth generation is a loose historical category associated with declarative logic, constraints and AI/expert systems. Generations do not determine whether an implementation uses an interpreter.

sources: MOE Computer Science Exit Exam · 2016 · Question 27

answer.explanation: CP04 explicitly places preprocessing before compilation proper and compilation before assembly. The assembler produces object files, which are linked into an executable and then loaded. D preserves that order, although it compresses linking/loading into one label and describes the final result loosely as target machine code.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Places the assembler before the compiler, reversing their stated order in CP04.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Attempts linking/loading before compilation and assembly have produced the required object files.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Places preprocessing after compilation and assembly, contrary to the conventional toolchain order.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Preserves preprocessing, compilation, assembly, linking and loading in the required sequence.

evidence.quote: In the conventional C++ toolchain: source → preprocessing → compilation proper → assembly → object files → linking → executable → loading → execution. Preprocessing handles directives such as #include; compilation may emit assembly; the assembler emits machine instructions in an object file. The linker resolves external symbols and combines object files and libraries. The loader places an executable and required components in memory and starts it.

module_refs.title: Computer Programming module
module_refs.quote: The compilation process of C++ program consists of the following steps. • edit source code  compile  link  execute (Editor) (Compiler) (Linker) (Loader) I. Program source code is entered into a file using a text editor. II. After the code has been entered, a compiler program is started that translates the source into an object code file. III. The object code file is linked with other object code files that come with the compiler and an executable file (or program) is created. IV. In order to execute the program, a program called the loader copies the executable file into the memory of the computer and sends an execute command to the CPU.

module_refs.title: Computer Programming module
module_refs.quote: Algorithm is an ordered set of unambiguous, executable steps, defining a terminating process. Important Properties of Algorithms - Correct: always returns the desired output for all legal instances of the problem. - Unambiguous: Each step must be clearly defined, having only one interpretation. - Precise: simple but efficient - Efficient: can be measured in terms of Time and Space - Finiteness: the execution of the algorithm must terminate in a finite amount of time for each possible set of input data/must have an end.

evidence.quote: A struct groups named members, possibly of different types. struct House{double price; int rooms;}; defines a type; House h{150000,3}; creates an object. h.rooms uses a dot. House* p=&h; p->rooms is equivalent to (*p).rooms. The pointer must refer to a live object before member access. A type definition alone does not create an ordinary instance.

module_refs.title: Computer Programming module
module_refs.quote: The for loop. Its format is: for (initialization; condition; increase) statement; 1, initialization is executed. Generally, it is a initial value setting for a counter variable. This is executed only once 2, condition is checked, if it is true the loop continues, otherwise the loop finishes and statement is skipped. 3, statement is executed. As usual, it can be either a single instruction or a block of instructions enclosed within curly brackets { }. 4, finally, whatever is specified in the increase field is executed and the loop gets back to step 2.

module_refs.title: Computer Programming module
module_refs.quote: Using continue and break Statements - The break statement skips the rest of the statements in the loop‟s block, jumping immediately to the next statement outside of the loop. - The continue statement is similar. It also skips the rest of the statements in the loop‟s block, but instead of terminating the loop, it transfers execution to the next iteration of the loop. It continues the loop after skipping the remaining statements in its current iteration.

questions.stem: Consider native C++ translation through assembly into an object file, stopping before linking. Which statement best describes the resulting object file’s instructions?

options.text: Machine-independent bytecode for a virtual machine

options.label: D
options.text: Native machine instructions in an object file

sources: Computer Science model exam · Question 67
University of Gondar model exam · Question 67

answer.text: D. Native machine instructions in an object file
answer.explanation: The specified native pipeline stops after the assembler produces an object file and before the linker combines objects and resolves external references. Its code is therefore native machine instructions in an object file. Machine-independent bytecode belongs to a different translation target, such as javac’s output, while a complete linked executable comes later in this C++ pipeline. Neither A nor B correctly names the specified result.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Machine-independent bytecode is a different target from the specified native object instructions.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: The pipeline stops before linking produces a complete executable.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Both A and B describe different targets or later stages.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: The assembler emits native machine instructions into an object file.

evidence.quote: In the conventional C++ toolchain: source → preprocessing → compilation proper → assembly → object files → linking → executable → loading → execution. Preprocessing handles directives such as #include; compilation may emit assembly; the assembler emits machine instructions in an object file. The linker resolves external symbols and combines object files and libraries. The loader places an executable and required components in memory and starts it.
Java javac produces bytecode, which a JVM interprets or compiles at runtime.

module_refs.title: Computer Programming module
module_refs.quote: The compilation process of C++ program consists of the following steps. • edit source code  compile  link  execute (Editor) (Compiler) (Linker) (Loader) I. Program source code is entered into a file using a text editor. II. After the code has been entered, a compiler program is started that translates the source into an object code file. III. The object code file is linked with other object code files that come with the compiler and an executable file (or program) is created. IV. In order to execute the program, a program called the loader copies the executable file into the memory of the computer and sends an execute command to the CPU.

evidence.quote: In the conventional C++ toolchain: source → preprocessing → compilation proper → assembly → object files → linking → executable → loading → execution. Preprocessing handles directives such as #include; compilation may emit assembly; the assembler emits machine instructions in an object file. Compilation uses multiple passes, so “whole program in one step” is not literally universal.

In order to execute the program, a program called the loader copies the executable file into the memory of the computer and sends an execute command to the CPU.

answer.text: A. Assembly language is machine independent
answer.explanation: Assembly is symbolic source tied to an instruction set; it is not machine independent. Before native execution, an assembler translates it into machine instructions. Those machine instructions are already in the target machine’s instruction format. Fifth generation is instead a historical language category associated with declarative logic, constraints and expert systems, rather than a universal hardware-performance requirement. Only A contradicts the specified language and execution model.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Assembly depends on the target instruction set, so this claim is false.

choices.label: D

evidence.quote: Machine instructions are conventionally first generation; symbolic assembly is second; general high-level languages such as C++ and Java are third. Database query and application generators such as SQL are conventionally fourth generation. Fifth generation is a loose historical category associated with declarative logic, constraints and AI/expert systems. Generations do not determine whether an implementation uses an interpreter.

In the conventional C++ toolchain: source → preprocessing → compilation proper → assembly → object files → linking → executable → loading → execution. Preprocessing handles directives such as #include; compilation may emit assembly; the assembler emits machine instructions in an object file. The linker resolves external symbols and combines object files and libraries. The loader places an executable and required components in memory and starts it.

Each program has a starting state, a list of operations to complete, and an ending point. This approach is also known as imperative programming. Structured Programming Languages Structured programming is a special type of procedural programming. It provides additional tools to manage the problems that larger programs were creating. Structured programming requires that programmers break program structure into small pieces of code that are easily understood. Object-Oriented Programming Languages Object-oriented programming is one the newest and most powerful paradigms. In object- oriented programs, the designer specifies both the data structures and the types of operations that can be applied to those data structures.

answer.text: D. To execute the body before its first test and repeat while the continuation condition is true.

questions.stem:
What is the output of the following C++ fragment code? int data[10] =
{5,10,15,20,25,30,35,40,45,50}; int i = 0; while (i <= 10) { if(data[i] % 10 == 0) { cout << data[i] << " "; i = i + 2; } }
questions.hint: Trace the initial state and each executed operation in order, preserving the requested output layout.
sources: Computer Science Exit Exam practice collection · Question 88

answer.explanation: Arrays are zero indexed (p.19), so initially data[0]=5. Its remainder on division by 10 is 5, not zero, so the if body is skipped. The only increment of i lies inside that skipped body. Therefore i stays zero, i<=10 remains true, and no cout is ever reached. The loop runs indefinitely with no output; it never reaches the potentially invalid index 10. Module support: PDF p. 19, PDF p. 11, PDF p. 8, PDF p. 9.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: No print occurs at the first iteration or later, so this odd-value sequence cannot appear.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: The loop never advances to data[1]=10.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: No array traversal occurs because i never changes.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Correct: nothing is printed, and the loop does not terminate.

evidence.quote: For n=1; n<=18; n+=2, print n unless n%7==0 then break: output is 1 3 5. A while(a>b) with fixed a=6,b=5 never changes its true condition. In data[10]={5,10,...,50}, i=0, advancing i only if data[i]%10==0 causes no progress because data[0]=5. It prints nothing and loops indefinitely; changing <=10 to <10 alone does not repair progress.

A built-in C++ array has a fixed number of same-type elements in contiguous storage: int a[4]={10,20,30,40};. Valid indices are 0 through 3. a[4] is outside the array; accessing it has undefined behavior. Java checks bounds and throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. Do not predict a C++ out-of-range value from nearby memory.

module_refs.title: Computer Programming module
module_refs.quote: Arrays - an array is a collection of fixed-size number of elements of the same type stored sequentially in memory. - An individual element of an array is identified by its own unique index (or subscript). - The number of elements must be an integer. - The size of the array is referred to as its dimension - Array in C++ is Zero indexed. Declaring of one-dimensional Array Syntax: elementstype arrayname [ size ];  You can use constants such as macro definitions or const ints as the sizes of arrays. Example: int num[5]; string fruit[3]; #define numstudents 100 or const int numstudents=100; double Score[numstudents] ; double Score[numstudents] ; Initialization of an Array - Arrays can be initialized at declaration time in two different ways: Syntax: elementstype arrayname[size] = {list each value separated by comma}; E.g int num[5]={1,2,3,4,5}; elementstype arrayname[ ] = { list with any number of values }; E.g int num[]={1,2,3,4,5}; string fruit[]={“Apple”,“orange”, “Mango”}; Accessing Array Elements - Each element could be accessed using an index into the array - When accessing an array, the index given must be a positive integer from 0 to n-1, where n is the dimension of the array.

While statement, and the for statement. The while loop: Its format is: while (expression) {statement;} First expression (called the loop condition) is evaluated. If the outcome is nonzero then statement (called the loop body) is executed and the whole process is repeated. Otherwise, the loop is terminated.

questions.stem: After a compiler reports a syntax error and before rebuilding, which action directly helps locate and repair its cause?

options.label: B
options.text: Ignore the error and continue execution

options.label: D
options.text: Check the code for typos or incorrect syntax

questions.hint: Apply the naming, type and syntax rules before deciding whether an option can be used as stated.
sources: Computer Science Exit Exam practice collection · Question 92

answer.text: D. Check the code for typos or incorrect syntax
answer.explanation: A syntax error violates the language grammar, so inspecting the relevant tokens and nearby declarations is the direct diagnostic step. The note recommends starting with the first useful compiler diagnostic, repairing the code and rebuilding afterward. Rewriting everything is unnecessary, ignoring the diagnostic leaves the defect in place, and a debugger is useful after a runnable program exists. The revised timing asks for inspection rather than the final verification step.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: A complete rewrite is unnecessary for locating a local grammar mistake.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Ignoring a compiler error leaves the cause unresolved.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: A debugger is useful after a runnable program exists.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Inspecting nearby tokens and declarations helps locate and correct grammar mistakes.

evidence.quote: A syntax error violates grammar; a type error can be syntactically well formed but rejected during semantic checking. A runtime error occurs during execution; a logic error gives the wrong behavior. A bug is a defect; debugging locates and corrects it. Read the first useful compiler diagnostic, inspect nearby tokens and declarations, repair and rebuild; a debugger is useful after a runnable program exists.

module_refs.quote: The compilation process of C++ program consists of the following steps. • edit source code  compile  link  execute (Editor) (Compiler) (Linker) (Loader) I. Program source code is entered into a file using a text editor. II. After the code has been entered, a compiler program is started that translates the source into an object code file. III. The object code file is linked with other object code files that come with the compiler and an executable file (or program) is created. IV. In order to execute the program, a program called the loader copies the executable file into the memory of the computer and sends an execute command to the CPU.

questions.stem: What is the difference between a compiler and an interpreter? Which is Java?
questions.hint: Use the cited language rules to separate the purpose of each construct from its implementation details.
sources: Computer Programming review questions · Question 1

answer.text: Compilers translate representations; interpreters execute them. Java uses bytecode compilation and JVM interpretation/JIT.
answer.explanation: CP04 says javac produces bytecode, then a JVM interprets or compiles it at runtime. A compiler translates rather than necessarily producing a complete native executable, while an interpreter executes a program representation. Java therefore cannot be reduced to exclusively compiled or interpreted.

evidence.quote: In the conventional C++ toolchain: source → preprocessing → compilation proper → assembly → object files → linking → executable → loading → execution. Preprocessing handles directives such as #include; compilation may emit assembly; the assembler emits machine instructions in an object file. The linker resolves external symbols and combines object files and libraries. The loader places an executable and required components in memory and starts it.

GCC documents the first four stages explicitly. A compiler need not emit a complete executable or even native machine code. Java javac produces bytecode, which a JVM interprets or compiles at runtime. Interpreters execute a program representation; “one source line at a time” is a beginner approximation. Compilation uses multiple passes, so “whole program in one step” is not literally universal.

questions.stem: What is the difference between = (assignment) and == (comparison)? Why is this a common mistake?
questions.hint: Use the cited language rules to separate the purpose of each construct from its implementation details.
sources: Computer Programming review questions · Question 2

answer.text: = assigns a value; == compares values for equality.
answer.explanation: CP06 describes assignment as replacing a variable’s value; CP10 describes equality as a value test. Confusing them can change state instead of testing it. In C++ a numeric assigned result can also convert to a condition, allowing an unintended assignment to alter control flow.

evidence.quote: In C++, simple assignment changes its left-hand object, and the assignment expression refers to that updated object. When an ordinary numeric assignment is used as a condition, the newly assigned value is converted to truth: zero is false and nonzero is true. Equality testing with == instead produces a Boolean result without assigning either operand. Confusing the two can both change program state and choose an unintended branch.

Relational and equality operators test values; && and || combine truth values; ! negates. In C++, zero converts to false and a nonzero number to true. Streams display bool as 0 or 1 unless boolalpha is set. With a=3,b=5, cout<<(a==b) prints 0.

questions.stem: What is the difference between while and do-while loops? When would you use do-while?

sources: Computer Programming review questions · Question 3

answer.text: while tests first; do-while runs once before testing. Use do-while for a mandatory first menu/input attempt.

evidence.quote: while(condition) checks before each body execution and may run zero times. do {body;} while(condition); runs the body once before checking; it repeats while the condition remains true. Use it when a menu or input attempt must occur at least once.

questions.stem: Why do we use functions? What are the benefits?
questions.hint: Use the cited language rules to separate the purpose of each construct from its implementation details.
sources: Computer Programming review questions · Question 5

answer.text: Functions decompose named tasks, enable reuse, reduce duplication and simplify understanding/testing.
answer.explanation: CP17 defines a function as grouping a named task and explains that reuse reduces duplication while independent functions are easier to understand and test. Decomposition localizes responsibilities and supports maintenance through those clearer units.

evidence.quote: A function groups a named task. C++ definition: int add(int a,int b){return a+b;}. Call it with add(x,y);, without parameter type declarations at the call site. Parameters are names in the definition; arguments are supplied expressions or values. A void function produces no return value but can have side effects and return; to exit early.

questions.stem: What is the difference between pass-by-value and pass-by-reference?
questions.hint: Use the cited language rules to separate the purpose of each construct from its implementation details.
sources: Computer Programming review questions · Question 6

answer.text: C++ value parameters copy; reference parameters alias caller variables. Java passes copied values, including references.
answer.explanation: CP18 makes a value parameter a separate initialized object, while int& aliases the caller variable and can change it directly. Passing a pointer copies an address and can change its target without rebinding the caller’s pointer. Java copies object references by value.

evidence.quote: A C++ value parameter is a separate object initialized from the argument. In func(int a,int b){a*=5;b+=5;return a+b;}, calling func(9,3) returns 53 and leaves the caller values 9 and 3 unchanged.

An int& parameter aliases the caller variable, so swap(int& a,int& b) changes both originals. An int* parameter copies an address; *p=value changes the pointed-to object, but p=anotherAddress only changes the local pointer. An array parameter int a[] is adjusted to int*: elements can change, and the length must be passed separately. Java always passes by value, including a copy of an object reference; it does not pass caller variables by reference.

questions.stem:
Assume that you are computer science expert and you need to develop large programs 
within short period of time. Finally, you have planned to provide portable program to the 
concerned body. Which type of programming language is preferable for the above 
scenario?
questions.hint: Use the cited language rules to separate the purpose of each construct from its implementation details.
sources: Computer Science Exit Exam · 2018 · Question 51

answer.text: A high-level language, with portability constraints checked.
answer.explanation: CP03 says high-level source is easier to read and often portable after recompilation if platform assumptions are avoided. That fits rapid development of a large program and a portable result better than instruction-set-dependent machine or assembly code. Portability remains conditional on the target environment; the answer is a preference, not an unconditional guarantee.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Low-level code retains instruction-set details and does not best match the stated readability/development and portability goals.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Machine-level code depends directly on the instruction set, opposing the requested portable-source preference.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: High-level source offers the note’s readability and conditional portability advantages for the stated scenario.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Assembly depends on the instruction set and is not the preferred abstraction for these development goals.

evidence.quote: Machine and assembly code depend on an instruction set. High-level source is easier to read and often portable after recompilation, provided it avoids platform assumptions. People can write both assembly and high-level programs. Python, Perl and PHP are commonly called scripting languages; C++ is conventionally compiled. These labels describe common use, not an absolute technical prohibition.

options.label: A
options.text: Overload function have same name but different parameters/type

options.label: C

options.label: D

sources: Computer Science Exit Exam · 2018 · Question 96

answer.text: Overloads share a name and differ in their parameter lists.

A missing condition in for(;;) acts as true.
A for loop is convenient for a known count but can also be condition controlled.
To print indices 0 through n-1, use i=0; i<n; ++i. Starting i=0 with i<5 and i+=2 prints 0 2 4.

break exits the nearest enclosing loop or switch. continue skips the rest of the current loop iteration: a for loop then runs its update; a while loop goes directly to its condition. return leaves the current function and may supply a result.
In main it ends the program normally.
A goto transfers to a label within its function; follow the label reached rather than reading lines in source order.
In the sequence a: print Graduating; goto b; c: print Year; goto a; b: print fourth;, entry at a prints Graduating fourth and reaches the end.
Year is not printed.
Structured alternatives usually make such logic easier to reason about.

Make a table with condition inputs, body output and updated values.
If odd i triggers continue, printing occurs twice.
With outer i=1; i<5; i+=5, the outer loop runs once; an inner j=10; j>i; --j prints nine times.
For n=1; n<=18; n+=2, print n unless n%7==0 then break: output is 1 3 5.
A while(a>b) with fixed a=6,b=5 never changes its true condition.
In data[10]={5,10,...,50}, i=0, advancing i only if data[i]%10==0 causes no progress because data[0]=5.
It prints nothing and loops indefinitely; changing <=10 to <10 alone does not repair progress.

A function groups a named task.
C++ definition: int add(int a,int b){return a+b;}.
Call it with add(x,y);, without parameter type declarations at the call site.
Parameters are names in the definition; arguments are supplied expressions or values.
A void function produces no return value but can have side effects and return; to exit early.
A method is a function associated with a class or object; methods can return values.
Modules group related responsibilities behind interfaces.
Reuse reduces duplication; independent functions are easier to understand and test.
A library provides reusable components; a framework also supplies an organizing structure and often calls application callbacks.

A C++ value parameter is a separate object initialized from the argument.
In func(int a,int b){a*=5;b+=5;return a+b;}, calling func(9,3) returns 53 and leaves the caller values 9 and 3 unchanged.
An int& parameter aliases the caller variable, so swap(int& a,int& b) changes both originals.
An int* parameter copies an address; *p=value changes the pointed-to object, but p=anotherAddress only changes the local pointer.
An array parameter int a[] is adjusted to int*: elements can change, and the length must be passed separately.
Java always passes by value, including a copy of an object reference; it does not pass caller variables by reference.

Overloads share a name but differ in parameter count or types/order.
Return type alone cannot distinguish them.

Choose a candidate using argument types, then required conversions; report ambiguity if there is no unique best match. int sum(int x,int y,int z=0) allows two or three arguments; defaults occupy trailing positions in ordinary declarations.
inline does not compel the compiler to copy a function body at a call.
Small frequently used functions may be good optimization candidates, but actual expansion is the optimizer’s decision.
Inline also has language linkage/definition rules, so it is not simply a speed command.

notes.title: Scope, lifetime and persistent static locals

blocks.text: Scope is where a name can be used; lifetime is when its object exists.
A local name is restricted to its block; an outer name may be shadowed.
A namespace/global variable is available where its declaration is visible, not magically in every file.
C++ ::name selects a global name hidden by a local one.
An automatic local is created anew on entry.
A static local is initialized once and retains its value across calls even though its name remains local.
If static x=0 changes by +1 when even and +2 otherwise, five calls return 1,3,5,7,9, whose sum is 25.
Namespace/static storage integers are zero initialized; an ordinary uninitialized local int has no usable assumed zero value.
Computer Programming module

notes.title: Recursion, base cases and call tracing

blocks.text: A recursive function calls itself directly or indirectly.
It needs a base case and progress toward it for all supported inputs. factorial(0)=1 and factorial(n)=n*factorial(n-1) for positive n. factorial(3) expands to 3*2*1*1=6.
Negative inputs require rejection or a separate definition; they do not reach zero under n-1.
Evaluate conditions before expanding a recursive call.
For if(n<m) return 0;, f(1,4) returns immediately; unreachable recursive branches add nothing.
Record each call’s local parameters and pending operation, then unwind returned values.
Recursion commonly uses smaller instances, but merely having a base-case branch does not prove it will be reached.
Computer Programming module
A built-in C++ array has a fixed number of same-type elements in contiguous storage: int a[4]={10,20,30,40};.
Valid indices are 0 through 3. a[4] is outside the array; accessing it has undefined behavior.
Java checks bounds and throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.
Do not predict a C++ out-of-range value from nearby memory.
A standard built-in array bound must be a compile-time constant; variable-length local arrays are compiler extensions. int a[5]={1,2,3}; fills the remaining elements with zeros.
An uninitialized automatic array of int is different. a[i] equals *(a+i), so elements can be accessed using pointer notation without explicitly writing brackets.
Computer Programming module
For a sum, start total=0 and add each element once.
For a maximum/minimum, initialize from a[0] only after confirming the array is nonempty.
For 50 inputs where nonpositive values are skipped, use a count-controlled loop and either if(x>0) total+=x; or continue for x<=0.
These constructs solve different parts of the task.
int a[R][C] has R rows, each with C elements. a[r][c] uses zero-based row then column.
Its element offset is r*C+c in row-major storage.
In the 4x4 matrix example, a[1][1]=6, a[2][3]=6 and a[3][3]=2.
In Java, length belongs to each array; a traversal ending at arr.length-2 visits fewer elements than a full traversal.

notes.title: C strings and C++ string objects

blocks.text: A C string is a character array ending in '\0'. "Hello" needs six char positions; strlen counts five visible characters and excludes the terminator. sizeof a fixed char array reports its allocated bytes, which can exceed strlen+1. cout<<a prints a terminated char sequence, not its numeric address.
<cstring> supplies strcpy(destination,source), strcat(destination,source), strlen and strcmp.
Supply enough destination capacity; strcmp returns zero for equal content, otherwise a sign, not necessarily exactly -1 or 1.
C++ std::string in <string> owns resizable text; + concatenates, == compares content, size()/length() counts stored characters and substr(start,count) extracts a segment.
Standard std::string has no Java-style toUpperCase() or trim() member.
Computer Programming module
int x=10; int* p=&x; stores x’s address in p. *p reads or writes x; &p is the address of the pointer variable itself.
With p=&a,q=&b, p=q redirects p to b and leaves a and b unchanged.
By contrast *p=*q copies the pointed-to value.
Never dereference an uninitialized, null or dangling pointer.
An array expression commonly converts to a pointer to its first element, but the array is not itself an assignable pointer variable.
A pointer-to-pointer int** pp=&p allows **pp to reach x. A void* can hold an object address but requires conversion to a suitable object pointer before dereferencing in C++.

notes.title: Scaled pointer arithmetic and dynamic allocation

blocks.text: If p points inside an array, p+k advances k elements, or k*sizeof(*p) bytes.

Under the explicit assumption sizeof(float)==4 and first address 7000, p+3 has numeric address 7012. cout<<p++ displays the old address then advances p; cout<<*p++ displays the old element then advances p. ++*p changes the element.
Pointer addition p+q is invalid; subtracting pointers within the same array gives an element distance.
Arithmetic must stay within an array or its one-past position; one-past may not be dereferenced.
C++ new T creates a dynamic object, delete releases it; new T[n] pairs with delete[].
Prefer resource-owning standard containers in real programs.
Allocation does not automatically initialize every primitive value unless initialization is requested.
Computer Programming module
A struct groups named members, possibly of different types. struct House{double price; int rooms;}; defines a type; House h{150000,3}; creates an object. h.rooms uses a dot.
House* p=&h; p->rooms is equivalent to (*p).rooms.
The pointer must refer to a live object before member access.
A type definition alone does not create an ordinary instance.
Aggregate initialization assigns members in declaration order.
Modern C++ permits default member initializers such as int rooms=3;.
C++11 list initialization rejects narrowing; a constant floating value exactly representable in the target floating type can be permitted, so 25.00 to float is not necessarily narrowing.
Use 25.0f for clarity and check the language version.
Structures can be copied, passed and returned; a structure cannot contain a full instance of itself, but may contain a pointer to its own type.

Include <iostream> and qualify std::cin/std::cout or introduce the names explicitly. cout is the standard output stream; << inserts values. cin is standard input; >> extracts formatted values. std::endl inserts a newline and flushes.
C++ names are case sensitive: Cout, Int and std: :cout are not equivalent valid spellings of cout, int and std::cout.
Read a full line with getline(cin,text).
After formatted numeric extraction, consume the pending newline before a line read when required.
Input failure must be tested before trusting a value.
Console output formatting matters: by default a double storing an exact 4 may print 4 rather than 4.0.
Text, spaces and newlines are part of an output trace.

notes.title: File streams, modes and safe reading

blocks.text: Include <fstream>. ofstream writes, ifstream reads, and fstream can do both.
The constructor’s default ofstream mode argument is ios::out; its ordinary effect is to create/truncate the file.
Distinguish the default mode argument from effective out|trunc behavior. ios::app places each write at the end; ios::ate initially seeks to the end; ios::binary requests binary mode.
Check if(!file) after opening.
Read using while(file>>record) or while(getline(file,line)), because end-of-file is discovered by an attempted read. while(!file.eof()) can process an invalid extra record.
Close or rely on stream destruction to release the resource. “ofstream” is a class, whereas <fstream> is the header.

Use <cmath> for sqrt, pow, floor and ceil; integer abs is also provided by <cstdlib>. sqrt(16)=4; pow(3,4)=81; abs(-7)=7. ceil(x) is the least integer-valued result >=x; floor(x) the greatest <=x. Thus ceil(-2.7)=-2 and floor(-2.7)=-3; truncation toward zero differs from floor for negatives.
C++ has no built-in exponentiation operator: ^ is bitwise XOR and ** is not a power operator.
To compute b^e for a nonnegative integer e, start r=1 and repeat r*=b exactly e times; b=4,e=3 gives 64.
Large powers and factorials can overflow fixed-width types; specify a valid input range.

notes.title: Correctness by logic, invariants and induction

blocks.text: To prove an implication P⇒Q, a direct proof derives Q assuming P; a contrapositive proves not Q⇒not P; a contradiction assumes the claim false and derives an impossibility.
A single counterexample disproves a universal claim.
Induction proves a base case and proves P(k+1) assuming P(k).
For sum=0,i=1; while(i<=n){sum+=i;++i;}, use invariant sum=(i-1)*i/2.
It holds initially.
Adding i gives i*(i+1)/2, then incrementing i restores the invariant.
Exit gives i=n+1 and sum=n*(n+1)/2.
Termination needs a separate decreasing nonnegative measure n-i+1 while the guard holds.
Assume n>=0 and no arithmetic overflow.
This connects mathematical proof to actual code.
Western University: program verification

A syntax error violates grammar; a type error can be syntactically well formed but rejected during semantic checking.
A runtime error occurs during execution; a logic error gives the wrong behavior.
A bug is a defect; debugging locates and corrects it.
Read the first useful compiler diagnostic, inspect nearby tokens and declarations, repair and rebuild; a debugger is useful after a runnable program exists.
Test ordinary, boundary and invalid inputs and trace the first point where actual state differs from expected state.
Exceptions transfer control to a matching handler for exceptional conditions; they do not make arbitrary undefined behavior recoverable.
Refactoring improves internal structure while preserving observable behavior.
Version control records changes, supports comparison and rollback; documentation explains use, design and maintenance assumptions.

Static typing checks types before execution; type inference can still infer a static type, as with C++ auto.
Dynamic typing checks operations using runtime values; it does not mean variables must have explicit static declarations.
Static typing does not always require explicit type annotations.
Java uses boolean, fixed-width numeric primitive types and references to objects.
Java String is immutable, substring(begin,end) uses an exclusive end, equals compares content and == compares references.
Java arrays have a length field.
Scanner nextInt() can leave a newline for nextLine().
C++ std::string is mutable and uses substr(start,count); the two APIs must not be merged.

notes.title: Check syntax and trace control flow

blocks.text: A program trace requires the complete code, and a diagram question requires its edges, conditions and labels.
When entry reaches the body rectangle before the decision diamond and a decision branch returns to the body, the body executes before the condition is tested.
This is a post-test do-while loop.

Match pointer-member names exactly: Cout/Cin, C1 and car_mode do not match cout/cin, c1 and car_model.

With valid C++ syntax for the stated assignments, the trace yields z=5 then a=1.
Printing Z when only z is declared refers to a different, undeclared identifier.
Use <0 for a less-than-zero comparison and the standard int main() declaration for a C++ entry point.
Check int and cout case, quotation marks and comma-expression punctuation before tracing a C++ expression.
Predict output only after the program and its execution conditions are clear.

Evaluate every choice against the language rules; more than one statement may be valid, or none may be valid.
Distinguish linking from loading.
Distinguish binary representation, machine code and executable files.
Assess class membership and possible initialization separately; both statements can be correct.
Check whether alternative short declarations are equivalent.
Check the C++ version and narrowing rules before evaluating an initialization.
Array subscripting and equivalent pointer access can refer to the same element.
Use the definition of static typing rather than equating it with explicit annotations.

A void function definition can be complete without returning a value; int myFunction(){} can compile, but reaching its end is undefined behavior.
A break statement exits the enclosing loop or switch.

Numeric scalar members become zero, and the elements of a character-array member become zero characters. A zero character at the beginning of such an array makes it an empty, terminated C string. notes.title: Keywords and names have different roles

blocks.text: A keyword is a reserved word with a predefined meaning in the language grammar. It cannot be repurposed as an ordinary variable or function name. An identifier is a name used to refer to a data object or function; its spelling must obey the identifier-character rules and avoid keywords.

notes.title: Java print and println preserve output layout

blocks.text: Java System.out.print writes the supplied value without automatically ending the line. System.out.println writes its value and then a line separator. Successive println calls therefore place their values on separate lines, even when each printed expression also contains a trailing space.
Java SE 17 — PrintStream print and println

notes.title: An assignment expression can accidentally become a condition

blocks.text: In C++, simple assignment changes its left-hand object, and the assignment expression refers to that updated object. When an ordinary numeric assignment is used as a condition, the newly assigned value is converted to truth: zero is false and nonzero is true. Equality testing with == instead produces a Boolean result without assigning either operand. Confusing the two can both change program state and choose an unintended branch.
C++ working draft — Assignment and compound assignment operators
